items.summary: NVIDIA released CUDA 13.5, marking general availability of the NVIDIA Vera Rubin GPU architecture for enterprise production alongside Windows on Arm support and updates across CUDA Python, CCCL, CUDA Tile, Nsight developer tools, and core math libraries such as cuBLAS, CUB, cusparse, and NVJPEG.
items.title: NVIDIA Ships CUDA 13.5 With Vera Rubin General Availability

items.summary: After Democrats posted historic midterm gains across Congress, state legislatures and governorships, candidates delivered victory speeches naming tech-related concerns. Many cited the influence of figures such as Elon Musk and the role of Big Tech in shaping information and the economy; some complained about AI deepfakes. The article presents a sample of statements from races across various jurisdictions.
items.title: Democratic Candidates Attack AI, Data Centers and Big Tech in Midterm Victory Speeches

items.summary: Two weeks ago, a school IT administrator asked Google how to block students from seeing AI Overviews in search results; no one responded. On Tuesday, Google announced it is declining to offer schools the option to disable AI Overviews and will instead require them to block all search access next year. The decision has stunned educators, parents, and researchers across the US. In a public response shared on X, Google argued that search, Gemini chatbot, and Gemini Notebook will be off by default while administrators can enable one, two, or all three services. A Washington University in St. Louis study found only about 42 percent of AI Overviews could be fully verified using their citations.
items.title: Google Refuses Schools an Off Switch for AI Overviews

items.summary: DuckDuckGo is pitching itself to schools following backlash over Google’s decision to keep AI features enabled by default. The company points to DuckDuckGo’s options for disabling AI, noting app installs rose 30% as users rejected forced AI Search. Meanwhile, educators continue seeking tools to remove AI from learning entirely.
items.title: DuckDuckGo Courts Schools After Google’s AI Policy Draws Backlash

items.summary: The organizers of PyTorch Day China 2026 have issued a final call for proposals. Submissions close November 10 at 23:59 China Standard Time, with the event held in Beijing on December 12. The program invites session presentations and lightning talks across five topic areas covering model training, efficient inference, PyTorch core and hardware acceleration, physical AI, and ecosystem applications.
items.title: PyTorch Day China 2026 Opens Call for Proposals

items.summary: Otilia Stretcu and Leijie Wang of Google Research describe Agile Deliberation, a framework that helps users collaboratively define subjective categories like healthy food or inspiring artwork by guiding them through concept scoping and iterative refinement. The authors report evaluating the system across 18 live user sessions lasting 1.5 hours each, finding it reduced cognitive fatigue and anxiety while producing classifiers with higher labeling consistency than standard baselines. They attribute these gains to replacing manual prompt engineering with direct feedback on borderline images routed into an automatic optimization loop. Code is open-sourced on GitHub.
items.title: Google Research Introduces Agile Deliberation for Subjective AI Classifiers

items.summary: Elon Musk spent about $474 million on the 2026 midterms, according to a New York Times tally through October 14. Democrats won control of both chambers Tuesday night. Forty-four of his candidates lost, including in key races; eighteen wins came only in seats Republicans were expected to win. His America PAC funneled money to Republican House and Senate candidates. SpaceX booked $6.78 billion in federal contracts through October 1 versus $3.8 billion all of 2024, as the party that controls Congress holds government purse strings.
items.title: Musk's Midterm Spending Bought Republicans Little

items.summary: An article published by Forethought, originally posted on its website and inspired by a conversation with Collin Burns, argues for distinguishing three types of alignment work that might be automated: empirical research (running experiments), conceptual research (theoretical understanding), and direct work making specific systems more aligned. The author notes these categories differ in automation needs and risks, suggesting they should be tracked separately. Most loss-of-control risk may come later, so the priority is keeping systems safe long enough to automate high-quality conceptual research; however, the author states being mostly uncertain about this, which argues for hedging by investing across all paths.
items.title: Forethought Proposes Tracking Three Types of Automated Alignment Work

items.summary: McDonald's reported a bigger-than-expected decline in comparable US sales of 0.2% in the quarter ended Sept 30, missing analysts' expectations for a 0.1% fall and marking its first such drop after five growth quarters. The company attributed the slide to consumers cutting back on dining out amid higher living costs. Global comparable sales rose 1.5%, while adjusted earnings reached US$3.57 per share from US$3.22 a year earlier.
items.title: McDonald's US sales fall for first time in six quarters amid value push

items.summary: Angel Song, a hair salon owner, welcomed barber Yuzzrie Adahar and his colleague into her salon as an example of how small businesses can support each other during rising rent pressures. The arrangement lets the barbers keep earning without renting a whole shop, keeps customers in the neighbourhood, and benefits the salon with more foot traffic. Song notes collaboration need not mean large investment.
items.title: Small business owner shares salon space with barbers amid rising rents

items.summary: Stephen Tan, writing in a forum letter dated Nov 3, recommends Singapore expand its smoke-free zones by learning from Tokyo. He recounts spending six days there without encountering second-hand smoke on streets marked with floor signs and enclosed smoking rooms. He notes that although Singapore piloted a no-smoking zone in Orchard Road, expansion plans have not materialised, and urges revisiting the initiative to protect non-smokers' right to clean air.
items.title: Singaporean urges adoption of Japan's smoke-free zone model

items.summary: Bitcoin fell to a seven-week low as bets of a Democratic sweep in the US midterms raised political uncertainty for crypto. It slid up to 2.8% to US$75,630.57 during Asia trading on Nov 4 and later traded around US$76,600. Analysts note broader market pressures from a Binance hack and shifting investor sentiment also weigh on the asset (45 words).
items.title: Bitcoin Dips on Democratic Midterm Hopes

items.summary: Leading the Future, described as the largest pro-artificial intelligence super PAC network, is leaving the midterm elections having spent roughly $26 million on primaries and cut its total spending by about $10 million while backing mostly safe candidates. It finished with just over $20 million remaining despite fielding many congressional candidates from both parties. Haworth of the Tech Oversight Project characterized the strategy as an influence play that failed to shape races, noting results fell flat in riskier contests such as Darline Graham's South Carolina Senate bid, where American Mission donated more than $2 million and she lost with 46.5 percent.
items.title: Pro-AI Super PAC Network Exits Midterms with Limited Impact

items.summary: Texas was the fastest-growing data center market and site of Big Tech's largest AI buildouts, but Democratic victories in September may jeopardize that position. Democrats James Talarico won a US Senate seat and Gina Hinojosa defeated incumbent governor Greg Abbott; at the state level, Democrats will take control of the Texas House for the first time in 24 years. Both winners made data centers central campaign issues. On September 21, Abbott directed a key regulator to halt permits, slowing or halting projects like Stargate Frontier (projected 1,820 megawatts) and Nexus Hubbard (planned 6,400 megawatts). Banks are growing cautious, raising concerns about ripple effects. However, no single office decides project outcomes—decisions involve cities, counties, and state offices—and local officials may resist sweeping restrictions.
items.title: Texas Political Shift Threatens AI Data Center Expansion

items.summary: Voters in Corpus Christi, Texas, overwhelmingly approved a citizen-led charter amendment imposing steep surcharges on the region's refineries and chemical plants during future droughts. The measure passed by roughly two to one despite heavy opposition spending from industry groups, marking a symbolic populist win amid historic statewide Democratic upsets. Under the plan, fees would trigger automatically when reservoirs fall below 30 percent full, rising with deeper drops or a declared water emergency. Campaigners say it reflects community frustration over industrial water use; city officials warn of legal challenges and note the amendment remains mostly symbolic for now.
items.title: Corpus Christi Voters Approve Drought Water Fees on Industrial Users

items.summary: On November 4, Bloomberg News reported that Apple reduced employee budgets for AI usage as part of a broader cost-control effort while seeking to expand AI use across operations. The company cut some engineers' daily AI spending from $300 to $200 last month and may lower it further to $100.
items.title: Apple Trims Employee AI Spending Amid Cost Controls

items.summary: A Shopify guide named by writer Brinda Gulati, published Feb. 11, 2026, lists 10 trending products to sell in 2026, drawn from U.S. merchant sales growth (June 2025 versus June 2024), Google Trends interest scores, Deloitte's ConsumerSignals report, and the National Retail Federation's 2026 retail forecast. The guide argues revenues grow with search volume and that Google can forecast retail up to three quarters ahead. Featured items include yoga mats, wrap skirts, soap, travel pants, reusable water bottles, home décor, pet supplies, blushes, protein powder (a $114 billion global category), and Lego sets. Each entry describes seasonal or rising interest patterns without supplying index values for individual products.
items.title: Shopify Guide Names Ten Trending Products for 2026 Sales

items.summary: After Democrats took control of both chambers of Congress, former IMF First Deputy Managing Director Gita Gopinath predicted a shift in President Donald Trump's tariff policy and greater Federal Reserve independence. She warned that America's fiscal deficit would remain a problem despite the political change.
items.title: Gita Gopinath Predicts Shift in Trump Tariff Policy After Midterm Upset

items.summary: Business Today TV's Karishma Asoodani reports that U.S. midterm elections are reshaping the political landscape, with Democrats making significant gains in key congressional races. The emerging results could increase scrutiny of President Donald Trump's tariff policies and complicate his trade agenda. Analysis explores what this means for unresolved India-US trade negotiations, market access and export prospects.
items.title: U.S. Midterm Results May Reshape India-US Trade Outlook

items.summary: A study using survey data from a private elite college challenges assumptions about campus self-censorship, finding that students with the most moderate views actually censor themselves more than others. The research suggests confidence and issue salience drive this pattern: those certain in their beliefs or viewing issues as important hold stronger views and censor less. Meanwhile, conservatives still self-censor at higher rates than liberals.
items.title: Study Finds Moderate Students Self-Censor Most on Campus

items.summary: The Guardian’s editorial argues that Britain should embrace closer EU cooperation through the “Made in Europe” regime rather than cling to Brexit. It notes Andy Burnham is expected later this month, at a summit with Ursula von der Leyen, to complete a treaty covering customs barriers for agricultural goods, youth mobility and integration with the carbon emissions trading scheme. The piece warns that without such an agreement, UK industries would face crippling trade barriers.
items.title: Guardian editorial backs UK-EU Made in Europe deal

items.summary: Aditya Chakrabortty argues that a coalition of billionaires and blue-collar voters built around Donald Trump has fractured under renewed class politics. He points to the midterms, describing them as a rejection of the president after wealthy donors poured billions into his campaigns while working- and middle-class voters resisted. Citing economists Fred Magdoff and John Bellamy Foster, he notes that workers' share of national income fell from 30% in the 1960s to 20% today. Harvard economist Jason Furman estimated AI infrastructure spending made up 92% of GDP growth for the first half of 2025, benefiting mainly a handful of firms. Chakrabortty highlights James Talarico's Texas win on an anti-datacentre platform and quotes him saying "The real fight in this country is not left versus right." He concludes that Democrats are shifting toward anti-billionaire politics.
items.title: Guardian columnist says class politics defeated Trump's billionaire alliance

items.summary: A UK minister says the government is considering restricting or banning smart glasses after concerns they are used to secretly film women, including viral videos from nights out. Safeguarding minister Satvir Kaur hinted at limiting sales to certain users and noted existing laws already apply in places like courts. NHS England and the Department for Education are also reviewing wearable technology.
items.title: UK government weighs smart glasses ban over secret filming

items.summary: Serbian authorities detained nine active police officers and one former officer on Wednesday for allegedly using excessive force against detainees during anti-corruption protests in Belgrade, the interior ministry said. The suspects served in an elite unit and were accused of torturing people held at a government compound on 14-15 August 2025. This marked the first major arrests tied to protest violence over two years. Vučić and SNS deny the accusations, which activists attribute to political pressure rather than misconduct alone.
items.title: Serbia Detains Police Officers Over Alleged Force Against Protesters

items.summary: A DW analysis of Tuesday's US midterms draws five takeaways from the Democrats taking control of both chambers of Congress. A post-election survey by news agency Associated Press found about 30% of voters saw democracy as their biggest problem, while about 70% felt Congress was not doing enough to check presidential power; analysts read this as a demand for stronger oversight that lets the new majority block funding and open investigations. The party's gains in Republican strongholds such as Texas and South Carolina, plus five DSA-endorsed House wins, suggest it remains electorally competitive. Republicans face an internal fight over Trumpism after he deflected blame on Truth Social. For Iran watchers, Trump's likely defeat is welcome news; for Europe, expert Ian Lesser told DW the outcome could reinvigorate trans-Atlantic dialogue and give Democrats more say over NATO policy and military funding.
items.title: Democrats' midterm gains reshape US power and Europe's outlook

items.summary: Australia say they have reviewed their heavy defeats to the All Blacks in both Bledisloe Cup tests and believe they have addressed many weaknesses ahead of a month of Nations Championship matches in Britain. Loosehead prop Angus Bell said the team had worked on pace and handling after losing 50-19 in Auckland and 43-21 in Sydney, with new coach Les Kiss guiding an unbeaten run before the blowout.
items.title: Wallabies Review All Blacks Loss Before England Test

items.summary: Bobby Pulido, a Tejano music singer aged 53, defeated Republican incumbent Monica De La Cruz in the November 3 midterm elections, flipping Texas's 15th Congressional District back to Democratic control. According to preliminary results reported by the Associated Press with 95% of ballots counted, he led her 62.32% to 37.68%, a margin of more than 20 percentage points. The victory ended four years of Republican representation in a South Texas district that President Donald Trump carried by 18 points in 2024. Pulido built his campaign around performing at quinceañeras, drawing on decades of playing music at community celebrations.
items.title: Tejano singer Bobby Pulido flips Texas's 15th District for Democrats

items.summary: FRANCE 24 Observers report that Chinese artificial intelligence chatbots suppress information about footballer Kylian Mbappé, who joked in October on a French podcast that the image he found funniest showed him atop what appeared to be Chairman Mao Zedong's body. The joke drew accusations of insulting China and prompted sponsors such as Dongpeng Group, Mengniu and Milkground to end partnerships with his club.
items.title: Chinese AI chatbots censor coverage of Mbappé's Mao remark

items.summary: Prime Minister Peter Magyar's government ordered the full release of Hungary's secret police 'agent files,' containing names and details of state security informants, on November 4. The move ends over three decades of debate after Fidesz repeatedly blocked publication since 2010, voting more than 30 times against it. Databases covering up to 60,000 out of an estimated 150,000 informants will go online, with confidentiality rules scaled back for future access. ABTL director Bendeguz Gergo Cseh cautioned that files cannot be fully trusted due to incomplete or destroyed documents. Historian Janos M. Rainer called the late release symbolic, while Krisztian Ungvary welcomed it as a chance for new research and honest reflection on Hungary's past under Fidesz rule.
items.title: Hungary Releases Decades-Old Communist Secret Police Informant Files

items.summary: A Mongabay map cross-referencing Compesa water supply schedules with IBGE census data finds that rationing in Recife falls along racial, gender and class lines. Of 311 locations surveyed across the Pernambuco capital in July 2026, 236 face chronic interruptions; peripheral areas receive about 17% of a regulatory benchmark set by ANA at more than 18 hours daily. Black women in low-income neighborhoods such as Ibura de Baixo and Linha do Tiro endure up to 15 consecutive days without water amid high flood risk, while affluent enclaves like Boa Viagem receive over 700 hours monthly. Residents report contaminated tap water causing illness and rising costs for bottled alternatives. The findings coincide with a partial privatization concession signed in April 2026 between the state government and BASA Saneamento, which critics warn may entrench inequities while defenders argue it funds expansion across all municipalities.
items.title: Racialized Water Rationing Deepens Inequality Across Recife

items.summary: Hungary released communist-era secret police files on Wednesday, identifying up to 60,000 informants and opening a path for the country in reckoning with its repressive past. The disclosure follows a September bill by Prime Minister Peter Magyar granting unrestricted public access to records first promised after the 1990 regime change. On that day, three of four document types dating before 1990 became accessible via nyitottaktak.hu; estimates suggest 50,000 to 60,000 agent names were made public overall, with a second batch covering about 9,000 informants due in February. Bendeguz Gergo Cseh, head of the Historical Archives of State Security Services (ÁBTL), said most informants did not shape national life and that records are incomplete and not always accurate. Historian Laszlo Eorsi called it better late than never, while cautioning against judging people solely by their names on the list.
items.title: Hungary Releases Communist-Era Informant Files, Naming Up to 60,000 Agents

items.summary: The Democrats won control of both chambers in the US midterm elections, flipping at least seven Senate seats and winning 237 races — 19 more than needed for a majority. President Donald Trump said he does not blame anyone, but acknowledged the war with Iran played a role; Vice-President JD Vance agreed that losing was caused by the conflict while defending it as worthwhile. With his approval below 40 per cent since April, some Republicans disagree, and strategist Doug Heye told Reuters voters felt unheard. Democrats now hold enough House votes to impeach Trump but would need Republican support in the Senate to convict. The new Congress is expected next year to investigate his administration. ABC/Reuters reported on the results this morning.
items.title: Democrats Win Midterms as GOP Blame Trump and Iran War

items.summary: Ecoganic 'red-tipped' bananas from Far North Queensland are now exported in regular fortnightly shipments of 1,200 kilograms to Japan after months of trials. Pioneered by Innisfail farmers Frank and Dianne Sciacca about 20 years ago, the accredited farming system uses natural ecosystems and minimal inputs. Japanese importer Tomoki Tokuda of Pacific Coast Asia Company says feedback has been excellent and hopes to raise volumes toward 3,000 kilograms within three years; so far the fruit is sold in two supermarkets and 60 restaurants nationwide. The Sciacca family noted export growth would require more growers than they currently have.
items.title: Queensland red-tipped bananas gain Japanese buyers

items.summary: Duran Duran return to Madrid’s Movistar Arena on November 6, described as a cross-generational phenomenon with enduring staying power. The band sold 100 million records and remains relevant across three or four career phases. Keyboardist Nick Rhodes, 64, says in a video call that he wants to vomit when asked about social-media numbers, adding he does not care even about the group's own figures but only cares whether a song is good rather than its view count. He also expresses disillusionment with today's music business as diabolical and money-driven.
items.title: Nick Rhodes Rejects Social-Media Metrics Amid Duran Duran's Madrid Return

items.summary: Iran's chief US negotiator Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf said Iranians had endorsed a "NO TO WAR" message after Republicans lost the midterm elections. Parliament speaker Ghalibaf posted the endorsement on X, warning that betrayal of public will would bring consequences. Trump acknowledged Tuesday that weak Republican results were partly due to war-related petrol price rises but denied regretting February's joint attack with Israel. In an interview he said part of the result reflected anger over gasoline costs. Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said US policy was unlikely to change, while President Pezeshkian stressed his government sought a dialogue-based resolution.
items.title: Iran's negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'

items.summary: Democrats' control of the US Senate gives them leverage over Federal Reserve appointments, potentially limiting President Trump's ability to install allies on its seven-member board. The shift may increase scrutiny of Chairman Kevin Warsh and slow administration-backed banking reforms. Economists at Monetary Policy Analytics noted limited Democratic support for his chairmanship.
items.title: Democratic Senate Control May Limit Trump's Fed Influence Amid Ongoing Risks

items.summary: Amazon announced that the Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 set records across savings, shopping volume, seller success and delivery speed. The event enabled over INR 2,800 crore in customer savings through deals, bank discounts, cashback, rewards and free Prime deliveries, while attracting over 393 crore customer visits already. Shopping volume rose more than 50% year-over-year, with more than 70% of shoppers coming from beyond the metros. Saurabh Srivastava, Vice President Amazon India, said customers chose Amazon.in to fulfill festive aspirations across smartphones and ethnic wear. The article is sourced by Deccan Chronicle.
items.title: Amazon Great Indian Festival 2026 Sets Record With Rs 2,800 Crore in Savings

items.summary: Brent crude traded over 8% lower at $94.91 a barrel while WTI was at $88.42, the article states. Democratic midterm victories led investors to expect President Donald Trump may favour diplomacy over military escalation in the US–Iran conflict, with Qatar mediating and reports of possible peace talks raising hopes for stabilised Middle Eastern oil supplies. Negotiations remain uncertain, as Iranian officials say the two sides are still far from an agreement.
items.title: Brent crude dips below $100 as Iran peace hopes rise after Democrats win midterms

items.summary: A report by Consumer Voice and Indiatech, part of the Ease of Vehicle Ownership Index (EVOI) 2026, ranked states on used-vehicle ownership procedures. Andhra Pradesh topped with a score of 5.9 out of 10; Kerala scored 5.7. Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal placed last. The report calls for unified digital records and standardised no-objection certificate processes.
items.title: Report Ranks Indian States on Ease of Vehicle Ownership

items.summary: The Cabinet is learnt to have approved a sixth extension for the Commission of Inquiry into the Manipur violence, pushing its report submission date to May 20, 2027. Constituted in September 2023 with an original November 2023 deadline, the commission was tasked with examining the causes and spread of the violence that began on May 3, 2023, including lapses by authorities. The extension gives it nearly four years to complete what was originally expected within months. Since then, the ethnic violence has claimed more than 300 lives and displaced thousands.
items.title: Cabinet approves sixth extension of Manipur violence inquiry panel, deadline set for May 2027

items.summary: After Democrats won a midterm sweep including Texas and Georgia, US markets split along industry lines on election day in 2025. Data-center stocks fell as Core Scientific dropped 3.5% while Iren slipped 3.6%. Solar makers rose instead: First Solar gained 7%, Sunrun added 6.1% and Enphase Energy was up 3.6%. Defense contractors such as Northrop Grumman also lost ground, while hospital operators like HCA Healthcare climbed 5.4%. Analysts said divided government could bring greater oversight of AI spending and clean-energy policy.
items.title: US Midterm Democrat Sweep Dips AI Stocks, Lifts Renewables
